class.name: NodePool
class.brief_description: Recycles nodes instead of instantiating them, for anything spawned by the hundred.
class.description:
Bullets, debris, enemies - anything whose cost is dominated by [method PackedScene.instantiate] rather than by what it does once it exists. [b]Pooling here means taking the node out of the tree, not disabling it.[/b] A node outside the tree does not exist for the physics server: it cannot collide, it costs no broadphase budget, and a "dead" body cannot be hit by accident. The alternative - freezing the body and disabling its processing - leaves it in the world and is a reliable source of bugs that are very hard to find. Give the pool either a [member scene] or a [member factory], then take nodes with [method acquire] and hand them back with [method release]: [codeblock] var bullet: Node = $BulletPool.acquire() bullet.global_position = muzzle.global_position [/codeblock] A pooled node keeps its state between uses, so it has to be reset on the way out and cleaned up on the way in. Give it [code]_on_acquired()[/code] and [code]_on_released()[/code] and the pool calls them; both are optional, and they are looked up by name because a pooled node is a [RigidBody2D] one moment and an [Area2D] the next, with no shared base class to declare them on. [codeblock] func _on_acquired() -> void: visible = true
func _on_released() -> void: visible = false linear_velocity = Vector2.ZERO [/codeblock]

method.name: acquire
method.description: Hands out a free node, creating one if the pool is empty, and parents it under [member container]. Returns [code]null[/code] only when the pool can create nothing: neither [member scene] nor [member factory] is set, or the factory did not return a [Node].

method.name: clear
method.description: Frees every node the pool owns, in use or not. Called automatically when the pool leaves the tree, because a node waiting in the free list has no parent and nobody else would ever free it.

method.name: get_active
method.description: Every node currently handed out. Built fresh on each call - keep your own list if you need it every frame.

method.name: get_total_created
method.description: How many nodes the pool has ever created. Watch it during play: if it climbs well past [member prewarm], the prewarm is too low for the real peak.

method.name: release
method.description: Returns a node to the pool. Safe from inside a physics callback or a signal: the node is marked free at once, but leaving the tree is deferred to the end of the frame, because removing a body mid-step is a hard engine error. That deferral means a released node is still parented and still reachable for the rest of the frame. Releasing it twice is a no-op rather than a double free.

method.name: release_all
method.description: Returns everything currently in the tree. This is how a round restarts without reloading the scene.

members.member: Where acquired nodes are parented. Empty means the pool itself. Point it at the level's actor root when pooled nodes should sit beside everything else rather than under a bookkeeping node.
Called with no arguments and must return a [Node]. Takes precedence over [member scene]; use it when a pooled node needs constructor arguments or a script attached from code.
How many nodes to create on [code]_ready[/code], so the first shot of the game does not pay for an instantiate.
Instantiated whenever the pool needs a new node and no [member factory] is set.
